Area.evidence_source: All participants indicated that their relationships with their parents prior to attempting suicide was distant owing to arguments and fights, the emotional unavailability of their parents as well as strict and controlling parenting strategies. All participants stated that they felt particularly disconnected from their fathers, and expressed sadness, anger and resentment at their fathers' lack of emotional involvement in their lives. Mark and Andrew said that their parents' lack of attention and affection made them feel alone and as a result of this, they wished to become 'independent' from their parents. All participants also indicated that they were subject to the rules and expectations of their parents, which made them feel 'trapped' or 'controlled'. Brian explained: 'My father would overpower the family; his rules or no rules. So that's why I felt that, you know, I couldn't breathe.' and Johan said: 'My dad was a corporal and he is extremely strict. He had a firm hand when he raised me. So speaking to him about failure, that you did something wrong, is impossible.' All participants said that they imagined that if they were dead they would be able to escape feeling trapped and they could then express their separateness and independence from their parents.
